negative_reviews.author: Mohammed Ali (Ali)
negative_reviews.text: To all the sheeps that fall for it and say this place has amazing food, you don’t know what good food is, and you don’t know anything because you never ate good food ever in your life, so you don’t know what delicious food taste like. I am very disappointed at this place not tasty at all, a shin cup pot noodle or ramen tastes way better than this place. Food took time to be served, wonky table, wobbly chairs and no service at all.

negative_reviews.author: Sheyda Gr
negative_reviews.text:
I have had two bad experiences in a row. Last time I went in and sat down near the kitchen and my food took over 35 minutes to come. There were not enough people to ensure they keep an eye on customers who sit in that area and nobody looked this way. I had to constantly try and catch someone’s eye although had my hand up all the time. Although I love the food but i don’t think I’ll go back as it was very disappointing .
Tonight I ordered the same food as I always do “Steak Tataki Ramen” and when it arrived it did “not” look like a Ramen, it was Dry, no juice at all. I had to put hot water in the bowl from the kettle with extra soya sauce to pretend like I am actually having a Ramen. Very upsetting to be honest coz these are very very basic stuff that can be done differently to change a customers experience.

gaps: Food % — 13.02% shown as Kobas reads it on 17/11 (deliveries 5,359.97 / gross 41,152.55), on Michael's instruction; likely low because not all deliveries are keyed yet (Kobas usage basis reads 25.34%)

issues: Sales rose week on week but missed target because trade is still down since reopening; covers rose 13.9%, bookings remain low and spend per head dipped slightly (England KPI meeting 17/11).

Mid week the site was trending at about £19K, up £5K on the week before but below the £27K to £30K pre fire level, with food cost at 20.6% and wages targeted at 26% to 28% (Birmingham Project Meeting 13/11).
Drinks variance increased because staff took drinks from the bar without ringing them through.
Loyalty sign ups declined, so the perks need promoting better.
Two negative reviews on Friday about food and wait times came during a full till crash when orders were taken by hand; overall ratings are back to 4.8 (Birmingham Project Meeting 13/11).
Food quality audits showed no red points, and Sophie carried out a mock EHO inspection and operational audit on 12/11.

Maintenance: a fridge was fixed on the meeting day, and Ross has the walk in freezer wall leak, the sushi hand wash sink losing hot water after 5 to 7 minutes, the vegetable fryer, the dry store fly zapper socket and lifting floor tiles.
A complaint about raw or partly cooked prawns was raised at Birmingham and Lakeside, and Sophie is investigating (Birmingham Project Meeting 13/11).
Too much stock was ordered at reopening, so orders will be kept mainly to frozen items.

The GM/HC meeting noted the Christmas menu (especially dessert) is selling, the stock count was 2.1% with some invoices missed, the dishwasher and fryer are fixed, and the ramen fridge and donburi heat lamp are broken (GM/HC meeting 16/11).
Promotions: 50% off first direct online delivery orders, the seasonal matcha menu and an outdoor bean bag game offering discounts or free gyoza.
Marketing budget was moved to Birmingham, bringing 58 bookings with booking events up from 121 to 570; the TTJ booking campaign stops on 20/11 (Weekly DPM meeting 17/11).

Repair the freezer wall leak, sushi sink hot water, fryer, fly zapper socket and dry store floor, and give arrival times - Owner: Ross Ward (24/11/2026)
